merger_description:
Count Limited (**Count**) currently has 1,607 fully owned shares in OBM Financial Services Pty Ltd (**O'Brien**), which is a 48.1% ownership on a fully diluted basis. Count proposes to acquire a further 83 fully paid ordinary shares in O'Brien, taking its ownership to 50.6% on a fully diluted basis.

Count is an ASX listed company, comprising an integrated network of over 120 firms providing accounting and wealth management services throughout the country (except for the Northern Territory). Count’s business is organised into three operating segments:

* Equity Partnerships (includes investments into firms that provide accounting, audit and assurance, taxation, financial planning services as well as business and corporate advisory services);
* Wealth (includes financial services and investments products provided by Australian Financial Services Licence holders); and
* Services (includes services that support the activities of accounting and financial planning firms that are both internal and external to Count’s network, including actuarial certificates, consulting, IT services, training and helpdesk and support services).

O'Brien has a single location in Ivanhoe, Victoria and provides the following services:

* accounting and tax services for individuals and business owners, with services including cashflow forecasting and management, budgeting, reporting, compliance and self-managed superannuation fund services; and
* personalised financial advice to individuals, families and retail and wholesale businesses, with services including investment advice, retirement planning and superannuation advice.

O'Brien operates as an authorised representative under the authorised financial services licence of Count Financial Limited, a Count subsidiary.

determination_table_content.details:
Count Limited (Count) applied for a notification waiver in respect of
its proposed acquisition of a further 83 fully paid ordinary shares in
OBM Financial Services Pty Ltd (O’Brien), taking its ownership to
50.6% on a fully diluted basis, as described in the transaction
documents provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).
Count currently owns 1,607 fully owned shares in O'Brien, which is a
48.1% ownership on a fully diluted basis.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Count, is an ASX listed company, comprising an
integrated network of over 120 firms providing accounting and
wealth management services throughout the country (except for the
Northern Territory). Count’s business is organised into three
operating segments:
• Equity Partnerships (includes investments into firms that
provide accounting, audit and assurance, taxation, financial
planning services as well as business and corporate
advisory services);
• Wealth (includes financial services and investments
products provided by Australian Financial Services Licence
holders); and
• Services (includes services that support the activities of
accounting and financial planning firms that are both
internal and external to Count’s network, including actuarial
certificates, consulting, IT services, training and helpdesk
and support services).
The target, O’Brien, has a single location in Ivanhoe, Victoria and
provides the following services:
• accounting and tax services for individuals and business
owners, with services including cashflow forecasting and
management, budgeting, reporting, compliance and self-
managed superannuation fund (SMSF) services; and
• personalised financial advice to individuals, families and
retail and wholesale businesses, with services including
investment advice, retirement planning and superannuation
advice.
O'Brien operates as an authorised representative under the
authorised financial services licence of Count Financial Limited, a
Count subsidiary.
Count and O'Brien overlap in the supply of financial advisory services
and accounting services.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
certain publicly available information, and had regard to the factors
in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010
(Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of financial
advisory services and accounting services in Victoria and
nationally is low and the increase in share of supply arising
from the Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative suppliers of financial advisory services
and accounting services in Victoria (including in the area
surrounding O’Brien’s offices) and nationally.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
